audit_status.source_base: Hebrew Deuteronomy / Devarim priestly support, prohibited divination, prophet-like-Moses, and false-prophet law, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for Levite portions, mobile Levite service, child sacrifice, divination and necromancy prohibitions, prophet like Moses, Horeb mediation, prophetic accountability, and failed-word test.

verses.restored: Levitical priests, all tribe of Levi, shall have no portion or inheritance with Israel; fire-offerings of YHWH and his inheritance they shall eat.

familiar.text: The priests the Levites, and all the tribe of Levi, shall have no part nor inheritance with Israel: they shall eat the offerings of the LORD made by fire, and his inheritance.

modern.text: The Levitical priests—indeed the whole tribe of Levi—shall have no portion or inheritance with Israel. They are to eat the offerings made by fire to the LORD; that is their inheritance.

original.text: לֹֽא יִ֠הְיֶה לַכֹּהֲנִ֨ים הַלְוִיִּ֜ם כָּל שֵׁ֧בֶט לֵוִ֛י חֵ֥לֶק וְנַחֲלָ֖ה עִם יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אִשֵּׁ֧י יְהוָ֛ה וְנַחֲלָת֖וֹ יֹאכֵלֽוּן

verses.restored: No inheritance shall be for him in midst of his brothers; YHWH is his inheritance, as he spoke to him.

familiar.text: Therefore shall they have no inheritance among their brethren: the LORD is their inheritance, as he hath said unto them.

modern.text: Although they have no inheritance among their brothers, the LORD is their inheritance, as He promised them.

original.text: וְנַחֲלָ֥ה לֹא יִֽהְיֶה לּ֖וֹ בְּקֶ֣רֶב אֶחָ֑יו יְהוָה֙ ה֣וּא נַחֲלָת֔וֹ כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר דִּבֶּר לֽוֹ

verses.restored: This shall be judgment/due of priests from people, from those sacrificing sacrifice, whether ox or sheep: one shall give priest shoulder, two cheeks, and stomach.

familiar.text: And this shall be the priest’s due from the people, from them that offer a sacrifice, whether it be ox or sheep; and they shall give unto the priest the shoulder, and the two cheeks, and the maw.

modern.text: This shall be the priests’ share from the people who offer a sacrifice, whether a bull or a sheep: the priests are to be given the shoulder, the jowls, and the stomach.

original.text: וְזֶ֡ה יִהְיֶה֩ מִשְׁפַּ֨ט הַכֹּהֲנִ֜ים מֵאֵ֣ת הָעָ֗ם מֵאֵ֛ת זֹבְחֵ֥י הַזֶּ֖בַח אִם שׁ֣וֹר אִם שֶׂ֑ה וְנָתַן֙ לַכֹּהֵ֔ן הַזְּרֹ֥עַ וְהַלְּחָיַ֖יִם וְהַקֵּבָֽה

verses.restored: First of your grain, new wine, and oil, and first of fleece of your flock you shall give him.

familiar.text: The firstfruit also of thy corn, of thy wine, and of thine oil, and the first of the fleece of thy sheep, shalt thou give him.

modern.text: You are to give them the firstfruits of your grain, new wine, and oil, and the first wool sheared from your flock.

original.text: רֵאשִׁ֨ית דְּגָֽנְךָ֜ תִּֽירֹשְׁךָ֣ וְיִצְהָרֶ֗ךָ וְרֵאשִׁ֛ית גֵּ֥ז צֹאנְךָ֖ תִּתֶּן לּֽוֹ

verses.restored: For him YHWH your Divine chose from all your tribes to stand to serve in name of YHWH, he and his sons all days.

familiar.text: For the LORD thy God hath chosen him out of all thy tribes, to stand to minister in the name of the LORD, him and his sons for ever.

modern.text: For the LORD your God has chosen Levi and his sons out of all your tribes to stand and minister in His name for all time.

original.text: כִּ֣י ב֗וֹ בָּחַ֛ר יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ מִכָּל שְׁבָטֶ֑יךָ לַעֲמֹ֨ד לְשָׁרֵ֧ת בְּשֵׁם יְהוָ֛ה ה֥וּא וּבָנָ֖יו כָּל הַיָּמִֽים

modern.text: Now if a Levite moves from any town of residence throughout Israel and comes in all earnestness to the place the LORD will choose,

modern.text: then he shall serve in the name of the LORD his God like all his fellow Levites who stand there before the LORD.

modern.text: They shall eat equal portions, even though he has received money from the sale of his father’s estate. Sorcery Forbidden (Acts 8:9–25)

modern.text: When you enter the land that the LORD your God is giving you, do not imitate the detestable ways of the nations there.

familiar.text: There shall not be found among you any one that maketh his son or his daughter to pass through the fire, or that useth divination, or an observer of times, or an enchanter, or a witch.

modern.text: Let no one be found among you who sacrifices his son or daughter in the fire, practices divination or conjury, interprets omens, practices sorcery,

original.text: לֹֽא יִמָּצֵ֣א בְךָ֔ מַעֲבִ֥יר בְּנֽוֹ וּבִתּ֖וֹ בָּאֵ֑שׁ קֹסֵ֣ם קְסָמִ֔ים מְעוֹנֵ֥ן וּמְנַחֵ֖שׁ וּמְכַשֵּֽׁף

familiar.text: Or a charmer, or a consulter with familiar spirits, or a wizard, or a necromancer.

modern.text: casts spells, consults a medium or spiritist, or inquires of the dead.

familiar.text: For all that do these things are an abomination unto the LORD: and because of these abominations the LORD thy God doth drive them out from before thee.

modern.text: For whoever does these things is detestable to the LORD. And because of these detestable things, the LORD your God is driving out the nations before you.

familiar.text: Thou shalt be perfect with the LORD thy God.

modern.text: You must be blameless before the LORD your God.

familiar.text: For these nations, which thou shalt possess, hearkened unto observers of times, and unto diviners: but as for thee, the LORD thy God hath not suffered thee so to do.

modern.text: Though these nations, which you will dispossess, listen to conjurers and diviners, the LORD your God has not permitted you to do so. A Prophet Like Moses (Acts 3:11–26)

verses.restored: A prophet from your midst, from your brothers, like me, YHWH your Divine will raise up for you; to him you shall listen.

familiar.text: The LORD thy God will raise up unto thee a Prophet from the midst of thee, of thy brethren, like unto me; unto him ye shall hearken;

modern.text: The LORD your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your brothers. You must listen to him.

original.text: נָבִ֨יא מִקִּרְבְּךָ֤ מֵאַחֶ֨יךָ֙ כָּמֹ֔נִי יָקִ֥ים לְךָ֖ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ אֵלָ֖יו תִּשְׁמָעֽוּן

verses.restored: According to all you asked from YHWH your Divine at Horeb on day of assembly, saying, Let me not continue hearing voice of YHWH my Divine, and this great fire let me not see again, lest I die.

familiar.text: According to all that thou desiredst of the LORD thy God in Horeb in the day of the assembly, saying, Let me not hear again the voice of the LORD my God, neither let me see this great fire any more, that I die not.

modern.text: This is what you asked of the LORD your God at Horeb on the day of the assembly, when you said, “Let us not hear the voice of the LORD our God or see this great fire anymore, so that we will not die!”

original.text: כְּכֹ֨ל אֲשֶׁר שָׁאַ֜לְתָּ מֵעִ֨ם יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֨יךָ֙ בְּחֹרֵ֔ב בְּי֥וֹם הַקָּהָ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר לֹ֣א אֹסֵ֗ף לִשְׁמֹ֨עַ֙ אֶת קוֹל֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהָ֔י וְאֶת הָאֵ֨שׁ הַגְּדֹלָ֥ה הַזֹּ֛את לֹֽא אֶרְאֶ֥ה ע֖וֹד וְלֹ֥א אָמֽוּת

verses.restored: YHWH said to me, They have done well in what they spoke.

familiar.text: And the LORD said unto me, They have well spoken that which they have spoken.

modern.text: Then the LORD said to me, “They have spoken well.

original.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלָ֑י הֵיטִ֖יבוּ אֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבֵּֽרוּ

verses.restored: A prophet I will raise up for them from midst of their brothers, like you; I will put my words in his mouth, and he shall speak to them all I command him.

familiar.text: I will raise them up a Prophet from among their brethren, like unto thee, and will put my words in his mouth; and he shall speak unto them all that I shall command him.

modern.text: I will raise up for them a prophet like you from among their brothers. I will put My words in his mouth, and he will tell them everything I command him.

original.text: נָבִ֨יא אָקִ֥ים לָהֶ֛ם מִקֶּ֥רֶב אֲחֵיהֶ֖ם כָּמ֑וֹךָ וְנָתַתִּ֤י דְבָרַי֙ בְּפִ֔יו וְדִבֶּ֣ר אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם אֵ֖ת כָּל אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֲצַוֶּֽנּוּ

verses.restored: It shall be, the man who does not listen to my words that he speaks in my name, I myself will require it from him.

familiar.text: And it shall come to pass, that whosoever will not hearken unto my words which he shall speak in my name, I will require it of him.

modern.text: And I will hold accountable anyone who does not listen to My words that the prophet speaks in My name.

original.text: וְהָיָ֗ה הָאִישׁ֙ אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹֽא יִשְׁמַע֙ אֶל דְּבָרַ֔י אֲשֶׁ֥ר יְדַבֵּ֖ר בִּשְׁמִ֑י אָנֹכִ֖י אֶדְרֹ֥שׁ מֵעִמּֽוֹ

verses.restored: But prophet who acts presumptuously to speak a word in my name that I did not command him to speak, or who speaks in name of other gods, that prophet shall die.

familiar.text: But the prophet, which shall presume to speak a word in my name, which I have not commanded him to speak, or that shall speak in the name of other gods, even that prophet shall die.

modern.text: But if any prophet dares to speak a message in My name that I have not commanded him to speak, or to speak in the name of other gods, that prophet must be put to death.”

original.text: אַ֣ךְ הַנָּבִ֡יא אֲשֶׁ֣ר יָזִיד֩ לְדַבֵּ֨ר דָּבָ֜ר בִּשְׁמִ֗י אֵ֣ת אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹֽא צִוִּיתִיו֙ לְדַבֵּ֔ר וַאֲשֶׁ֣ר יְדַבֵּ֔ר בְּשֵׁ֖ם אֱלֹהִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֑ים וּמֵ֖ת הַנָּבִ֥יא הַהֽוּא

verses.restored: If you say in your heart, How shall we know word YHWH did not speak?

familiar.text: And if thou say in thine heart, How shall we know the word which the LORD hath not spoken?

modern.text: You may ask in your heart, “How can we recognize a message that the LORD has not spoken?”

original.text: וְכִ֥י תֹאמַ֖ר בִּלְבָבֶ֑ךָ אֵיכָה֙ נֵדַ֣ע אֶת הַדָּבָ֔ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹא דִבְּר֖וֹ יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: When prophet speaks in name of YHWH and thing does not happen or come, that is word YHWH did not speak; in presumption prophet spoke it. You shall not be afraid of him.

familiar.text: When a prophet speaketh in the name of the LORD, if the thing follow not, nor come to pass, that is the thing which the LORD hath not spoken, but the prophet hath spoken it presumptuously: thou shalt not be afraid of him.

modern.text: When a prophet speaks in the name of the LORD and the message does not come to pass or come true, that is a message the LORD has not spoken. The prophet has spoken presumptuously. Do not be afraid of him.

original.text: אֲשֶׁר֩ יְדַבֵּ֨ר הַנָּבִ֜יא בְּשֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֗ה וְלֹֽא יִהְיֶ֤ה הַדָּבָר֙ וְלֹ֣א יָב֔וֹא ה֣וּא הַדָּבָ֔ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹא דִבְּר֖וֹ יְהוָ֑ה בְּזָדוֹן֙ דִּבְּר֣וֹ הַנָּבִ֔יא לֹ֥א תָג֖וּר מִמֶּֽנּוּ

translation_notes: Levitical dependence creates communal obligations of material support and equal access to service.
The mobile Levite may join central service according to desire and receive an equal portion.
The divination list reflects ancient Israelite boundaries around authorized revelation; it must not be used to persecute harmless spiritual, cultural, psychological, or religious practices today.
The prophet like Moses arises from within Israel and belongs first to Jewish covenant interpretation; later claims must not erase that context.
Fulfillment is one test of prophecy, but Deuteronomy 13 also insists that signs alone are insufficient.
The death penalty for false prophecy is source-preserved and categorically barred from modern enforcement.
safety_note: Do not use Deuteronomy 18 to execute alleged false prophets, persecute minority religions, criminalize harmless spiritual practice, or appropriate the prophet-like-Moses promise against Jewish interpretation. Center protection of children, material support for servants of community, accountable speech, and freedom from fear of failed predictions.
